decision.message:
Escalation: Flat 4, 8-12 Juniper Mews, Vellumford (tenant Elian Voss, landlord Owen Vale, contractor Gareth Lune, Copper Finch Plumbing).

What was reported (3 Sept, E001): a dripping kitchen tap, and a bathroom hot tap that drips and is hard to shut off. Rainwater also drips through the bathroom vent in heavy rain, and damp patches have appeared on the smaller bedroom's ceiling and wall.

Landlord (4 Sept, E004): "Yes, please proceed." In the same email he asked us to check what building insurance may cover and to review the flat's history. He says roof leaks have happened repeatedly and some of the damage looks severe. Nobody has answered this in 10 days. E005 records that it was not done, and the 5 Sept update to him (E012) does not mention it.

Visit: all the issues went to the plumber as one referral (E008). He attended late morning on 12 Sept (E020). On 11 Sept he had also written "Job was done today", then corrected it to "Booked for tomorrow" (E014, E015). The invoice (E022, A1, dated 14 Sept) covers only a new kitchen mixer tap and a new brass insert and chrome head on the basin hot tap. It has no amount, no VAT basis and no work date, and it shows the wrong property: Flat 4, 28 Larkspur Quay, Brindlewick. No visit report is on file. Nothing shows the vent leak or the bedroom damp was looked at (E021). No quote for a replacement mixer is on record; the tenant reported a drip.

Decisions that need you:
1. How to deal with the water coming in through the vent and the bedroom damp. This looks like a roof or building matter, not plumbing, and may need a roofer or the block's management. It has had no inspection for 11 days.
2. How to answer the landlord's building-insurance and roof-history request (E004). I cannot check insurance or speak to the insurer.
3. Whether the kitchen mixer replacement was within the "proceed" approval, once we have the amount.

Already done in this turn (routine): the plumber has been asked for a corrected PDF invoice for this address with the amount, VAT and work date, plus a visit report covering the vent and damp. Reply by Tue 16 Sept. The tenant has had an update, safety advice and a question on whether the leak and damp are still active. Reply by Tue 16 Sept; we told the tenant they will hear from us by Wed 17 Sept.

Recommendation: send the landlord a holding update on Mon 15 Sept. Acknowledge the unanswered insurance and history request, give the status, and say the vent and damp have not yet been inspected. Then arrange the right trade to inspect the roof/vent and damp, with his agreement. Do not forward or deduct the invoice until it is corrected and checked against the approval.
decision.rationale: The tap work is evidenced only by an invoice that names a different property and has no amount, so it cannot go to the landlord (refinement 1; manual 0a.3–0a.4). The bigger open items need a person. Water has been coming in through the vent with damp on the bedroom ceiling and wall for 11 days with no inspection (E001, E021). The landlord says roof leaks keep happening and the damage looks severe, and asked for an insurance and history check that has gone unanswered for 10 days (E004, E005, E012). Choosing the right trade, dealing with building or insurance questions and judging whether the mixer replacement was in scope go beyond routine handling (manual s.5: water through a ceiling, spend beyond approval). Following refinement 6, the routine contractor chase and the tenant update go out now in alsoSend.
decision.expectedOutcome: A supervisor takes ownership of the leak and damp response and the landlord's insurance and history question. The plumber sends a corrected invoice and a visit report. The tenant confirms whether the leak and damp are still active.

decision.message:
Handover: Flat 4, 8-12 Juniper Mews, Vellumford (tenant Elian Voss, landlord Owen Vale). This needs a decision from you.

1. Water ingress has not been looked at. On 3 Sept the tenant reported rainwater coming through the bathroom vent in heavy rain, and damp patches on the ceiling and wall of the smaller bedroom (E001). Everything went to Copper Finch Plumbing as one referral (E008). Gareth Lune attended on 12 Sept (E020). His invoice text covers only the two taps (E022, A1), and nothing on file shows the vent or the damp were checked (E021). The leak is now 11 days old with no assessment. We do not know if water is near the bathroom extractor or any other electrics. This looks like a roof or building issue rather than plumbing, so a different trade or the building's managing agent may be needed.

2. The landlord's own request has had no answer. On 4 Sept Owen Vale said "Yes, please proceed" and also asked us to check what building insurance may cover and to review the flat's history of repeated roof leaks. He said some of the damage looked severe (E004). Neither has been done (E005), and our 5 Sept update did not mention them (E012). He has now waited 10 days.

3. The invoice cannot be used yet. It has no amount and no VAT basis. It shows the property as "Flat 4, 28 Larkspur Quay, Brindlewick" (A1), not Juniper Mews. It also invoices a new kitchen mixer tap where the tenant reported a dripping tap. No quote for a replacement is on record, so we need to check that against what the landlord approved. Do not forward it or deduct it from rent yet.

4. Keys: the tenant offered key collection (E007), but on the day the tenant let the plumber in (E020). Please check the key log to confirm any agency keys are back.

I have sent these today: a chase to Gareth Lune for a visit report (vent and damp included) and a corrected PDF invoice by Tue 16 Sept, and a message to Elian Voss asking about the taps and the leak, with interim safety advice.

Decisions needed from you: (a) who inspects the vent leak and damp (roofer, surveyor or block management) and how urgently; (b) how we answer Owen Vale on insurance and roof-leak history, and what we can tell him today; (c) whether the kitchen mixer replacement goes back to him as a priced item before the invoice is processed.
decision.rationale: Approval to attend is on record (E004) and the visit happened (E020). Normally the next step would be the invoice and a landlord update, but three things block that. First, a water-ingress problem with damp, possibly near the bathroom vent's electrics, has gone unassessed for 11 days (E001, E021). Second, the landlord's explicit request about insurance and repeated roof leaks has gone unanswered for 10 days, and he described the damage as severe (E004, E005, E012). That needs someone with authority over insurance and building matters. Third, the invoice conflicts with the case on property, amount and scope (A1, E022), so it cannot be forwarded. Under the rules, a leak with damp that may affect health or electrics, and roof-level building matters, go to a person. Routine requests go out in the same turn: the plumber is asked for the missing report and corrected invoice, and the tenant gets safety advice and is asked to confirm the fix.

The plumber sends a report and a corrected invoice, and the tenant reports the current state of the taps and the leak.

Escalation: Flat 4, 8-12 Juniper Mews, Vellumford (tenant Elian Voss, landlord Owen Vale, contractor Gareth Lune, Copper Finch Plumbing).

What was reported (3 Sept, E001): a dripping kitchen tap, and a bathroom hot tap that drips and is hard to shut off. Rainwater also drips through the bathroom vent in heavy rain, and damp patches have appeared on the smaller bedroom's ceiling and wall.

Landlord (4 Sept, E004): "Yes, please proceed." In the same email he asked us to check what building insurance may cover and to review the flat's history. He says roof leaks have happened repeatedly and some of the damage looks severe. Nobody has answered this in 10 days. E005 records that it was not done, and the 5 Sept update to him (E012) does not mention it.

Visit: all the issues went to the plumber as one referral (E008). He attended late morning on 12 Sept (E020). On 11 Sept he had also written "Job was done today", then corrected it to "Booked for tomorrow" (E014, E015). The invoice (E022, A1, dated 14 Sept) covers only a new kitchen mixer tap and a new brass insert and chrome head on the basin hot tap. It has no amount, no VAT basis and no work date, and it shows the wrong property: Flat 4, 28 Larkspur Quay, Brindlewick. No visit report is on file. Nothing shows the vent leak or the bedroom damp was looked at (E021). No quote for a replacement mixer is on record; the tenant reported a drip.

Decisions that need you:
1. How to deal with the water coming in through the vent and the bedroom damp. This looks like a roof or building matter, not plumbing, and may need a roofer or the block's management. It has had no inspection for 11 days.
2. How to answer the landlord's building-insurance and roof-history request (E004). I cannot check insurance or speak to the insurer.
3. Whether the kitchen mixer replacement was within the "proceed" approval, once we have the amount.

Already done in this turn (routine): the plumber has been asked for a corrected PDF invoice for this address with the amount, VAT and work date, plus a visit report covering the vent and damp. Reply by Tue 16 Sept. The tenant has had an update, safety advice and a question on whether the leak and damp are still active. Reply by Tue 16 Sept; we told the tenant they will hear from us by Wed 17 Sept.

Recommendation: send the landlord a holding update on Mon 15 Sept. Acknowledge the unanswered insurance and history request, give the status, and say the vent and damp have not yet been inspected. Then arrange the right trade to inspect the roof/vent and damp, with his agreement. Do not forward or deduct the invoice until it is corrected and checked against the approval.
final.rationale: The tap work is evidenced only by an invoice that names a different property and has no amount, so it cannot go to the landlord (refinement 1; manual 0a.3–0a.4). The landlord says roof leaks keep happening and the damage looks severe, and asked for an insurance and history check that has gone unanswered for 10 days (E004, E005, E012). Choosing the right trade, dealing with building or insurance questions and judging whether the mixer replacement was in scope go beyond routine handling (manual s.5: water through a ceiling, spend beyond approval). Following refinement 6, the routine contractor chase and the tenant update go out now in alsoSend.
